The claim states that the intersection is valid if: 1) xy is within bounds [-epsilon, 1+epsilon], 2) xyz is in front of the camera (z > -epsilon), and 3) t > -epsilon. Source [S1] explicitly lists the validity check as `valid = _is_in_bounds(xy) & _is_in_front_of_camera(xyz) & _is_positive_t(t)`. Source [S2] notes explicitly state: 'Validate the projection: check if `xy` is in bounds $[-<epsilon>, 1+<epsilon>]$, if `xyz` is in front of camera ($z > -<epsilon>$), and if $t > -<epsilon>$.' Source [S3] notes state: 'Determine validity: the projection is valid if it is in bounds, in front of the camera (xyz z-coordinate positive), and t is positive.' While S3 uses 'positive' (implying > 0) and S1/S2 use '> -epsilon', the core conditions (bounds, front of camera, positive t) are consistent across all sources, and S2 explicitly matches the epsilon bounds mentioned in the claim. Therefore, the evidence supports the claim.
